# NearEats

> Find restaurants, cafes and bars near you — with what's open right now, diet options, step-free access, real walking time and one-tap directions. One-time $1.99, no subscription.

NearEats is an iPhone app that finds places to eat and drink around you and shows the details that decide where you actually go: whether a place is open right now (or closing in 25 minutes), whether it does vegan, halal, kosher or gluten-free, whether you can get in without steps, how long the walk really is, and whether it takes cards. It merges OpenStreetMap and Apple Maps so a venue found in both appears once with the best details from each. There is no account and no sign-up. It is a directory of facts, not a review platform — it has no ratings, reviews or user photos, because no open data source provides them honestly.

## Key Facts

- Platform: iOS (iPhone, iOS 18+)
- Pricing: $1.99 one-time purchase on the App Store. No subscription, no in-app purchases, no ads, no free tier
- Data sources: OpenStreetMap (Overpass API) and Apple Maps (MapKit), merged and de-duplicated
- Privacy: no account, no sign-up, no email. Saved and visited places stay on the device; search results are cached locally for 30 days. Anonymous usage analytics including session replay are sent to PostHog (EU) — see https://neareats.12f.dk/privacy-policy.html. Nothing is sold
- Languages: 49
- Developer: 12F ApS, Denmark (https://12f.dk/)
- Website: https://neareats.12f.dk/
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/neareats-restaurant-finder/id6754101006

## Features

- Restaurants, cafes and bars — three categories, switched with one control
- Clustered map with a synced list; tap a pin to highlight the venue
- Smart opening status read against the current time: "Open now", "Closes in 25 min", "Opens at 17:00"
- Open-late filter for the evening question
- Diet options per venue: vegan, vegetarian, halal, kosher, gluten-free, dairy-free, organic
- Accessibility: wheelchair access and accessible toilets, including a red warning when a venue is NOT accessible
- Warning badges for decision-critical negatives, shown ahead of the positives: cash only, not wheelchair accessible
- Amenities: outdoor seating, Wi-Fi, takeaway, delivery, drive-through, dog-friendly, family-friendly, air conditioning, microbrewery, fireplace
- Michelin and Bib Gourmand award badges where a venue has one
- Route-accurate walking time, not straight-line distance
- "Surprise me" — one tap picks a venue for you
- Search and filter by name, cuisine or feature
- "Been here" journal to mark places worth returning to
- One-tap directions, plus the venue's website and phone number
- 30-day on-device cache for speed and poor connections
- Dark mode, Dynamic Type and VoiceOver support

## What NearEats deliberately does not have

- No ratings, reviews, star scores or user photos — no free data source provides them honestly, so the app shows facts instead
- No account, sign-up or login
- No ads, and no paid placement: no venue can pay to appear higher in a list
- No subscription

## Blog

Practical guidance on finding somewhere good to eat, published at https://neareats.12f.dk/blog/ (RSS: https://neareats.12f.dk/feed.xml).

- [How to find good food in a city you don't know](https://neareats.12f.dk/blog/how-to-find-good-food-in-a-city-you-dont-know/) — travel-tips, 2026-08-27. A method for finding somewhere good to eat in an unfamiliar city — read the street before the reviews, check opening hours and distance before you commit, and use the details that actually predict a good meal.
